title: Surface-approximating sequence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $(f_m)_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $f_m:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. The sequence is surface-approximating for $A$ if every $f_m$ is infinitely continuously differentiable, takes values in $[0,1]$, and each coordinate derivative $x\mapsto Df_m(x)[e_i]$ is square-integrable with respect to standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$; moreover, $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|f_m(x)-\mathbf{1}_A(x)|\,d\gamma_n(x)\to 0$ as $m\to\infty$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a sequence of functions from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$
